**Mechanism verified on the live cluster (not taken on trust):**

The body asserts the remote login shell is zsh and that a `nomatch` abort
swallows LATER chained probes. Direct probe of charmander:

- Login shell CONFIRMED zsh: `SHELL=/usr/bin/zsh`, `$0 = zsh`, passwd
  field 7 = `/usr/bin/zsh`.
- Six discriminating cases run on charmander against a fixture dir holding
  one real `.log` under a subdir plus a nomatching top-level glob:
  - **T1 — one command, two glob args (the actual #1336 shape): BROKEN.**
    The whole command is skipped; the subdir that DID match is never read.
    rc=1.
  - **T2 — pipeline (`grep <nomatch-glob> | tail -3`): BROKEN, AND rc=0.**
    The pipeline never runs, output is empty, and the reported status is
    ZERO — so the caller cannot even detect it by exit code. This is the
    incident's literal shape and the sharpest part of the trap.
  - **T3 — `&&`-chained: later command does NOT run.** rc=1.
  - **T4 — `;`-chained: the later command DOES run.**
  - **T5 `grep -r <dir>` and T6 `find <dir> -name '*.log' -exec grep ... {} +`:
    both correct, rc=0** — the body's two proposed glob-free fixes are
    verified working, not just plausible.

**One factual correction carried into planning (not a Goal change).** The
body's "Why this matters" paragraph attributes the danger to the
semicolon-chained compound command — *"When several probes are chained in
one `ssh "...; ...; ..."`, a nomatch abort in an early probe means the
LATER probes never execute at all."* T4 falsifies that: `;`-chained
siblings survive. The real, verified mechanism is (a) a SINGLE command
carrying multiple glob arguments loses the entire command when ANY one of
them nomatches — which is exactly what cost the #1336 poll cycle — plus
(b) `&&`-chaining, and (c) pipelines, which additionally report rc=0 and
so fail undetectably. The entry will document the verified mechanism; the
per-probe-isolation advice survives on its own merits (it also bounds the
`&&` and rc-masking cases), and the read-side UNKNOWN-not-absent corollary
is unaffected and if anything strengthened by the rc=0 finding.

The `## Goal` is unchanged and needs no refinement: "add a gotchas.md entry
for a remote-shell trap that makes SSH monitoring probes fail silently-ish"
describes exactly this work.

**MUST-FIX 1 — the v1 `rc=0` claim was mechanically WRONG.** v1 said the piped
form meant "pipeline skipped ... rc=0". The critic measured on local zsh, and
the orchestrator then re-measured on charmander (round-2 probes P1-P4), that:
only the glob-bearing STAGE is skipped — the rest of the pipeline RUNS on empty
input (`P1: CONSUMER_RAN` printed) — and the pipeline's exit status is the LAST
stage's, so `| tail -3` gives rc=0, `| wc -l` gives rc=0 and prints `0`, but
`| grep <pat>` gives **rc=1**. v1's framing was both internally incoherent (a
"skipped" pipeline returning 0) and actively misleading: a reader seeing rc=1
from a piped probe would have ruled OUT the nomatch trap when it was exactly
that. RESOLVED in v2: the entry now states the consumer dependence explicitly
and concludes "rc neither confirms nor clears the trap". New acceptance
criterion A8 forbids the `pipeline skipped` phrasing; kill criterion 2 now
requires P1-P4 to be re-run at implementation time, because this sentence is
the one most likely to be wrong.

**MUST-FIX 2 — the prescribed `grep -r <pat> <dir>` was not equivalent to the
glob form it replaces.** Three undisclosed semantic drifts, all confirmed on
charmander (P5): bare `grep -r` recurses (vs top-level-only `*.log`), drops the
filename filter entirely, and re-adds `path:` prefixes plus
`grep: ...: binary file matches` noise that the incident's own `-h` suppressed
— which changes what a downstream `| tail -3` parse sees. The critic also
caught that T5 had verified `grep -rhoE`, not the bare `grep -r` the RULE
sentence actually prescribed, so v1's "(both verified correct...)"
over-claimed for the schematic form. RESOLVED in v2: the prescribed form is
`grep -rhoE --include='*.log' <pat> <dir>`, verified clean at rc=0 on
charmander (P6); the entry now discloses the bare-`grep -r` drift inline. New
acceptance criterion A9 requires `--include=` (or an equivalent disclosure
clause) in the landed text.

**MUST-FIX 3 — v1 contained a scope self-contradiction.** Its allowed-deviations
list permitted "adding a `.claude/agent-memory/` long-form companion note"
while the same plan's must-ask list forbade "any change to a file other than
`.claude/rules/gotchas.md`" and its Reproducibility Card promised "files
changed: exactly one". An implementer could take either reading, and the
allowance was off-convention besides (agent-memory files are written by their
owning agents, not as plan overflow). RESOLVED in v2: struck from allowed,
stated explicitly under must-ask.
